title: Counting what you do not want
objectives: Count by subtracting the unwanted cases from the total.
Count the union of two overlapping groups with inclusion and exclusion.

screens.title: Counting what you do not want
screens.prose: Some counts are hard head-on but easy from the other side. We will count everything, then take away what we do not want.
Two fair dice give 36 outcomes, one cell each. The row is the first die and the column is the second.
screens.question: How many of the 36 outcomes show no 6 at all?

hints.text: Which cells contain a 6?
Row 6 and column 6 hold every outcome with a 6.
With no 6, each die shows 1 to 5. That is a 5 by 5 block.

feedback.correct: Each die has 5 faces that are not 6: $5 \times 5 = 25$.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Keep only the cells where neither die is a 6.

byKey.one-die: You removed row 6 only. A 6 on the second die counts too, so column 6 goes as well.
byKey.corner-twice: You took away row 6 and column 6 in full, 12 cells. They share (6, 6), so only 11 cells go.
byKey.at-least-one: That counts the outcomes with a 6. The question asks for those with none.

explain.text: No 6 means each die shows 1 to 5, so $5 \times 5 = 25$ cells. They form the block in the top left.

screens.prose: Now the other side. Tap a cell to shade it, and tap it again to clear it.
screens.question: Shade every outcome with at least one 6.

hints.text: A 6 can be on the first die, the second die, or both.
Row 6 is a 6 on the first die.

feedback.correct: Eleven outcomes: row 6 and column 6, with (6, 6) once.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Shade row 6 and column 6, and nothing else.

byKey.no-corner: You left out (6, 6). Two 6s is still at least one 6.

explain.text: You shaded 11 cells: row 6, column 6, and (6, 6) once. That is $36 - 25$: everything minus the outcomes with no 6.

screens.prose: Three dice give too many outcomes to shade. No 6 is the **complement** of at least one 6: every outcome is in exactly one of the two. So count everything, count the complement, and subtract.
screens.question: How many outcomes of three dice show at least one 6?

hints.text: How many outcomes are there in all? How many have no 6?
With no 6, each die has 5 faces left.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count all outcomes and the outcomes with no 6, then subtract.

byKey.added: You counted 36 outcomes with a 6 on each die and added them. Outcomes with two or three 6s were counted more than once.
byKey.none: That is the complement, the outcomes with no 6. Subtract it from the total.
byKey.all: That is every outcome. Take away the 125 with no 6.
byKey.per-die: You added 6 for each die. Count whole outcomes of three dice: $6 \times 6 \times 6$ in all.

screens.prose: A 4-digit PIN uses the digits 0 to 9, and digits may repeat. So 0070 and 1234 are both allowed.
screens.question: How many PINs contain at least one 0?

hints.text: Count the PINs with no 0 at all.
With no 0, each place has 9 digits to choose from.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count every PIN, then take away the PINs with no 0.

byKey.added: You counted 1000 PINs with a 0 in each place and added them. A PIN such as 0070 was counted more than once.
byKey.none: That is the complement, the PINs with no 0.
byKey.all: That is every PIN. Take away those with no 0.
byKey.one-place: That counts PINs with a 0 in one fixed place. The 0 can be in any place.

screens.prose: A desk has 30 traders. The diagram shows how many trade only equities, only FX, both, or neither. Tap a region to select it.
screens.question: Tap every region that counts as trading at least one of the two.

hints.text: A trader who trades both still trades at least one.
The overlap holds the traders who do both.
Everything inside the two circles counts. Only the outside does not.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Select every region inside at least one circle.

byKey.exactly-one: You left out the overlap. Trading both is still trading at least one.
byKey.none: The outside region holds the 4 who trade neither.

explain.text: At least one is everything inside the circles: $11 + 7 + 8 = 26$. It is also everything minus neither: $30 - 4 = 26$.

screens.prose: A bigger desk has 40 traders. 22 trade equities and 15 trade FX. Of these, 9 trade both.
screens.question: How many trade at least one of the two?

widget.label: Traders who trade at least one

hints.text: Where are the 9 who trade both? Are they inside the 22, the 15, or both?
The 9 sit inside both circles, so both totals include them.
$22 + 15$ counts the 9 twice. Take them away once.

feedback.correct: Add the circles, then take the overlap away once: $22 + 15 - 9 = 28$.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. The 9 who trade both are inside each circle's total.

byKey.double: You added 22 and 15. The 9 who trade both are in each total, so you counted them twice.
byKey.removed-twice: You took the 9 away twice. That leaves only the traders who do exactly one, but those who do both count too.
byKey.neither: That is the number who trade neither: $40 - 28$.
byKey.minus-all: You took both circles from 40: $40 - 22 - 15 = 3$. That takes the 9 away twice. Find the traders inside the circles first: $22 + 15 - 9$.

explain.text: Adding 22 and 15 counts the 9 in the overlap twice. Taking them away once gives $22 + 15 - 9 = 28$. So 13 trade only equities and 6 only FX.

screens.prose: Call the regions $a$ (only $A$), $x$ (both) and $b$ (only $B$). Write $|A|$ for the number in $A$; GCSE writes $n(A)$. We want the rule behind your 28.
screens.question: Put the lines of the argument in order.

lines.text: Each circle's total includes the overlap: $|A| = a + x$ and $|B| = b + x$.
Add them: $|A| + |B| = a + b + 2x$. The overlap is counted twice.
Take the overlap away once: $|A| + |B| - x = a + b + x$.
The right side is every region inside the circles: $|A \cup B| = |A| + |B| - |A \cap B|$.

hints.text: Start by writing each circle's total in terms of the regions.
The overlap $x$ belongs to both circles.
Totals, add, take $x$ away once, then read off the union.

feedback.correct: Adding the circles counts the overlap twice, so we take it away once.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Write the totals first, then add them, then fix the double count.

byKey.union: The union line reads off the line before it, so it comes last.

explain.text: Each circle's total holds the overlap, so adding them counts $x$ twice. Removing it once leaves $a + b + x$, every region inside the circles. That is the **inclusion and exclusion** rule.

screens.prose: A stock closes up (U) or down (D) each trading day, never flat. A week's pattern lists its five moves, such as UUDUD.
screens.question: How many weekly patterns have at least one down day?

widget.label: Patterns with at least one down day

hints.text: Which patterns have no down day at all?
With no down day, every day has only one choice: U.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count every pattern, then take away the one with no down day.

byKey.all: That is every pattern. UUUUU has no down day, so it goes.
byKey.exactly-one: That counts patterns with exactly one down day. At least one also allows two, three, four or five.
byKey.none: That is the complement: UUUUU, the one week with no down day.
byKey.added: You added 2 for each day. Each day multiplies the patterns: $2^5$ in all.

explain.text: There are $2^5 = 32$ patterns, and only UUUUU has no down day. So $32 - 1 = 31$ weeks have at least one down day.

screens.prose: A backtest covers 250 trading days. Signal X fired on 60 days and signal Y on 45 days. Both fired on 20 of those days.
screens.question: On how many days did neither signal fire?

hints.text: First find the days when at least one signal fired.
The 20 days in the overlap are inside both totals.
At least one: $60 + 45 - 20 = 85$. Neither: $250 - 85$.

feedback.correct: Neither is everything minus at least one: $250 - 85 = 165$.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count the days with at least one signal, then take them from 250.

byKey.double: You took away 60 and 45 in full. The 20 overlap days were taken away twice.
byKey.union: That is the number of days with at least one signal. The question asks for neither.
byKey.minus-overlap: You took away only the 20 days when both fired. Days with one signal also count as a signal day.

explain.text: At least one signal fired on $60 + 45 - 20 = 85$ days. So neither fired on $250 - 85 = 165$ days. Inclusion and exclusion gave the union, and the complement gave the rest.

ideas: At least one is everything minus none. Count the complement, then subtract.
Two overlapping groups: add them, then take the overlap away once.
The complement of at least two is none or exactly one, not just none.

formula.name: Inclusion and exclusion
formula.note: With complements: at least one $=$ all $-$ none.

summary.trap: Adding two groups that overlap counts the overlap twice. Take it away once.

quiz.prose: Think of the whole numbers from 1 to 100.
quiz.question: How many are divisible by 2 or by 5?

options.why: You added 50 and 20. Multiples of 10 are divisible by both, so you counted them twice.
That is the even numbers only. Odd multiples of 5, such as 15, count too.
That is the count divisible by neither.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add the two groups, then take away the numbers in both.

explain.text: 50 are even and 20 are multiples of 5. The 10 multiples of 10 are in both, so $50 + 20 - 10 = 60$.

quiz.prose: A coin is tossed three times.
quiz.question: How many of the possible sequences contain at least one head?

widget.label: Sequences with at least one head

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count all sequences, then take away the one with no head.

byKey.all: That is every sequence. TTT has no head.
byKey.exactly-one: That counts exactly one head. Two or three heads are at least one too.
byKey.added: You added 2 for each toss. Each toss multiplies: $2^3 = 8$ in all.

explain.text: There are $2^3 = 8$ sequences, and only TTT has no head. So 7 have at least one.

quiz.prose: A stock closes up or down on each of the five days of a week.
quiz.question: How many weekly patterns have at least two down days?

options.why: That is at least one down day. Weeks with exactly one down day must go too.
You took away one week for none and one for exactly one. Exactly one down day happens in 5 weeks, not 1.
That is exactly two down days. At least two also allows three, four or five.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The complement of at least two is none or exactly one.

explain.text: This is the edge case: the complement of at least two is none or exactly one. One week has no down day, and 5 have exactly one. So $32 - 1 - 5 = 26$.

quiz.prose: Two cards are dealt from a standard 52-card deck. There are $\binom{52}{2} = 1326$ possible hands, and $\binom{48}{2} = 1128$ of them have no ace.
quiz.question: How many two-card hands contain at least one ace?

widget.label: Hands with at least one ace

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Subtract the hands with no ace from all hands.

byKey.double: You chose an ace, then any other card: $4 \times 51$. A hand with two aces was counted twice, once for each ace.
byKey.none: That is the number of hands with no ace.

explain.text: All hands minus the hands with no ace: $1326 - 1128 = 198$. Choosing an ace then any card gives 204, because the 6 two-ace hands are counted twice.
